problem: Large language models lack reliable uncertainty quantification, limiting their use in high-stakes domains where knowing when the model is uncertain is critical.
approach: Interprets prompts as textual parameters in a Bayesian statistical model and uses Metropolis-Hastings through LLM Proposals (MHLP), a novel MCMC algorithm, to perform Bayesian inference over these prompts and their downstream predictions.
contribution: Demonstrates improved predictive accuracy and uncertainty quantification on LLM benchmarks by combining prompt optimization with principled Bayesian inference, providing a turnkey modification for closed-source LLM pipelines.

problem: LayerNorm layers in transformers hinder mechanistic interpretability by introducing nonlinearities and increasing component interconnectedness, while their true role at inference time remains poorly understood.
approach: Removes all LayerNorm layers from GPT-2 models with minimal validation loss increase and tests whether standard interpretability techniques work better without LayerNorm.
contribution: Shows LayerNorm-free GPT-2 models can function with only +0.03 cross-entropy loss on GPT-2 XL, enabling more precise mechanistic interpretability research while clarifying LayerNorm's limited role in language modeling.

problem: Combining quantization and pruning for LLM compression is challenging because they have conflicting requirements: quantization favors compact weight distributions while pruning benefits from high variance.
approach: Proposes Optimal Brain Restoration (OBR), a training-free framework using second-order Hessian objectives and surrogate approximation to align pruning and quantization through error compensation between both methods.
contribution: Achieves only 1.4 perplexity degradation on Llama2-7B with W4A4KV4 quantization and 50% sparsity, delivering up to 4.72x speedup and 6.4x memory reduction compared to FP16-dense baseline.

problem: Model merging in weight space is limited to matching architectures and sizes, making heterogeneous merges infeasible when combining models of different scales or designs.
approach: Encodes model weights into a smooth latent space using a transformer-based VAE trained with a two-stage compression curriculum, enabling cross-architecture operations before decoding back to weights.
contribution: Latent-space interpolation is more robust than direct weight-space averaging and yields stronger downstream performance when merging models of different sizes, providing a scalable architecture-agnostic recipe.

problem: Current concept-based explainability methods neglect out-of-distribution robustness, while 3D-aware classifiers lack interpretability analysis despite their improved OOD performance.
approach: Designs CAVE (Concept Aware Volumes for Explanations), a robust classifier that learns sparse concepts from 3D object representations and proposes 3D Consistency (3D-C) metric using ground-truth meshes to measure spatial concept consistency.
contribution: Achieves competitive classification performance while discovering consistent and meaningful concepts across images in various OOD settings, unifying interpretability and robustness.

problem: Diffusion-based policies for multi-task robot manipulation suffer from high computational costs and scaling challenges due to large model sizes and data requirements.
approach: Introduces Skill Mixture-of-Experts Policy (SMP), which learns a compact orthogonal skill basis with sticky routing to compose actions from task-relevant subsets of experts, using a variational training objective.
contribution: SMP achieves higher success rates than large diffusion baselines with markedly lower inference cost on real dual-arm manipulation tasks, demonstrating a practical path toward scalable multi-task learning.

problem: Evaluating language models on structured data querying and transformation (JSON) lacks standardized benchmarks, making it difficult to assess LLM capabilities on these practical tasks.
approach: Introduces jqBench, automatically created from Stack Overflow and Spider datasets, with both instruction-based and example-based evaluation modes for JSON querying and transformation tasks.
contribution: Provides comprehensive benchmark showing Claude Opus 4.1 achieves 77% on jqStack and 81% on jqSpider, reveals documentation access doesn't improve performance, and shows automatic feedback is crucial.

problem: Generative models struggle to synthesize rare or fine-grained visual concepts even though they produce high-quality general content.
approach: Proposes ImageRAG, a training-free method that uses Vision Language Models to identify generation gaps, retrieves relevant reference images, and guides generation through conditioning on retrieved images.
contribution: Consistently improves rare and fine-grained concept generation across three datasets and three generative models without requiring RAG-specific training.

problem: While Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) improves generalization, its impact on membership privacy in machine learning models remains unexplored.
approach: Analyzes membership inference attacks against SAM-trained models through memorization and influence scores, and models SAM under a perfectly interpolating linear regime.
contribution: Shows SAM is more prone to membership inference attacks than SGD despite lower test error, with theoretical proof that SAM's geometric mechanism reduces variance and guarantees higher membership leakage.

problem: Time series foundation models lack explicit utilization of domain-specific textual and image context, hindering cross-domain generalization and zero-shot inference capabilities.
approach: Introduces Aurora, a multimodal time series foundation model that uses Modality-Guided Multi-head Self-Attention to inject text and image guidance into temporal representations, and employs Prototype-Guided Flow Matching for generative forecasting.
contribution: Demonstrates strong cross-domain generalization and zero-shot inference capabilities on TimeMMD, TSFM-Bench, and ProbTS benchmarks with state-of-the-art multimodal and unimodal performance.

problem: Current low-rank architectures for LLM pre-training suffer from compromised performance, high computational overhead, and limited memory savings.
approach: Proposes CR-Net (Cross-layer Low-Rank residual Network), which exploits inter-layer activation residuals' low-rank properties through a dual-path architecture and develops specialized activation recomputation.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art low-rank frameworks across model scales from 60M to 7B parameters while requiring fewer computational resources and less memory.

problem: Entropy-regularized reward optimization for fine-tuning generative models, while solved in continuous spaces, remains largely unexplored for discrete generative models like diffusion-based LLMs.
approach: Proposes Discrete Adjoint Matching (DAM), which introduces discrete adjoint as an estimator for optimal solutions formulated on discrete domains, extending Adjoint Matching to discrete diffusion processes.
contribution: Demonstrates DAM's effectiveness on synthetic and mathematical reasoning tasks for discrete generative model fine-tuning.

problem: The geometry of vision-language model embeddings remains poorly understood despite their remarkable success in aligning images and text.
approach: Operationalizes the Iso-Energy Assumption (exploiting cross-modal redundancy) with an Aligned Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) that encourages energy consistency during training while preserving reconstruction quality.
contribution: Reveals vision-language embedding structure where bimodal atoms carry alignment signal, unimodal atoms explain modality gap, and restricting vector arithmetic to bimodal subspace improves retrieval.

problem: Current attribution methods for transformers focus on simple concepts and multi-layer perceptron neurons, overlooking attention mechanisms and complex concept analysis.
approach: Introduces Scalable Attention Module Discovery (SAMD), a concept-agnostic method mapping complex concepts to specific attention heads via cosine similarity, and Scalar Attention Module Intervention (SAMI) for concept adjustment.
contribution: Demonstrates SAMD on concepts of varying complexity, showing attention module locations remain stable before and after LLM post-training.

problem: Document-level knowledge graph construction is constrained by high LLM costs for large-scale corpora and incomplete/inconsistent graphs from smaller models.
approach: Introduces SynthKG, a multi-step data synthesis pipeline generating high-quality document-KG pairs, and Distill-SynthKG, which fine-tunes smaller LLMs on synthesized data to streamline multi-step processes into single-step generation.
contribution: Distill-SynthKG surpasses larger models in KG quality and excels in retrieval and question-answering tasks; proposes novel graph-based retrieval framework for RAG.

problem: Synthetic data augmentation with diffusion models requires 10-30x data increase to improve performance and lacks targeted augmentation strategies.
approach: Augments only data not learned early in training with faithful images containing same features but different noise, using theoretical analysis of a two-layer CNN to motivate the strategy.
contribution: By augmenting only 30%-40% of data, achieves up to 2.8% generalization improvement across various architectures and optimizers, including surpassing SAM with SGD on CIFAR-100.

problem: Rotation estimation methods need new approaches for learning rotations in neural networks with efficient continuous representations.
approach: Reformulates rotation estimation (Wahba's problem) using special unitary matrices (SU(2)) to derive multiple solutions and proposes novel continuous representations for learning rotations.
contribution: Develops novel methods for rotation representation in neural networks validated through extensive experiments.

problem: Multi-view evidential learning tends to assign more evidence to data-rich classes, leading to biased evidence and unreliable uncertainty estimation.
approach: Proposes Fairness-Aware Multi-view Evidential Learning (FAML) with adaptive priors based on training trajectories and class-wise evidence variance constraints, plus opinion alignment for multi-view fusion.
contribution: Achieves more balanced evidence allocation and improves both prediction performance and reliability of uncertainty estimation on six real-world multi-view datasets.

problem: Video editing tasks typically require task-specific architectures and customizations, limiting flexibility and unification of diverse editing approaches.
approach: Proposes UNIC (UNified In-Context Video Editing), which represents all editing tasks as token sequences and jointly models them using DiT's native attention, introducing task-aware RoPE and condition bias.
contribution: Unifies diverse video editing tasks within a single model in an in-context manner without requiring task-specific adapter designs.

problem: Large language models demonstrate a radical decoupling between text and authorial intent, enabling hiding of meaningful text within different coherent text of the same length, raising AI safety concerns.
approach: Presents Calgacus, a protocol where LLMs encode hidden messages within coherent cover text of identical length using steganographic techniques.
contribution: Demonstrates that 8-billion-parameter LLMs can encode messages locally on a laptop in seconds, illustrating text-integrity risks for content authenticity.

problem: Masked Diffusion Language Models have computational inefficiencies from non-informative mask and padding tokens that limit training and inference efficiency.
approach: Proposes Deletion-Insertion Diffusion (DID) language models, formulating token deletion and insertion as discrete diffusion processes with score-based approach and efficient dynamic programming for training.
contribution: Improves efficiency and flexibility over MDLMs with better modeling performance, sampling quality, and faster training/inference, while supporting variable-length sequences without padding.

problem: Generating high-performance sparse CUDA code requires domain-specific architectural knowledge and accounting for irregular sparse data structure properties.
approach: Proposes SparseRL framework combining deep reinforcement learning with pre-trained language models, using sinusoidal embeddings for sparse matrices and hierarchical reward functions.
contribution: Improves compilation rate by 20% and achieves 30% faster generated code on average for SpMV tasks; shows significant gains for SpMM tasks.

problem: System prompts in LLMs are largely unstudied despite their importance, with most research focusing on task-specific prompts.
approach: Proposes SPRIG, an edit-based genetic algorithm that iteratively constructs general system prompts from prespecified components to maximize performance across diverse task types.
contribution: A single optimized system prompt performs on par with task-specific prompts, generalizes across model families and parameter sizes, and is complementary to task-level optimizations.

problem: Long Chain-of-Thought reasoning in LLMs incurs substantial memory overhead from Key-Value Cache that existing quantization methods fail to handle effectively.
approach: Proposes Progressive Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization (PM-KVQ) with progressive bit-width reduction and block-wise memory allocation, plus calibration strategy with positional interpolation.
contribution: Addresses cumulative error and short-context calibration issues, enabling efficient KV Cache quantization for long-CoT LLMs.

problem: Unsupervised reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for LLM improvement lacks clear understanding of potential and limitations of intrinsic reward methods.
approach: Presents unified theoretical framework showing intrinsic reward methods trade uncertainty for performance, with empirical analysis revealing distinct failure modes.
contribution: Provides insights into URLVR tradeoffs, shows collapse is not inevitable in domain-specific regimes, and identifies early intrinsic reward dynamics as lightweight trainability indicator.

problem: The expressive power of state space models as alternatives to transformers remains poorly understood from a formal computational perspective.
approach: Analyzes SSM expressiveness through fragments and extensions of linear temporal logic over finite traces, distinguishing fixed-width vs unbounded precision models.
contribution: Shows SSM expressive capabilities vary substantially by gating mechanism, with quantized models staying within regular languages and unbounded-precision models capturing non-regular languages.

problem: Existing 3D generation methods struggle to create animatable rigged geometry while rigging techniques lack fine-grained structural control.
approach: Introduces Stroke3D, a two-stage pipeline using Skeletal Graph VAE and DiT to generate skeletons from 2D strokes and text, then synthesizes textured meshes via TextuRig dataset and skeleton-mesh alignment optimization.
contribution: First work to generate rigged 3D meshes conditioned on user-drawn 2D strokes, enabling intuitive workflow for creating ready-to-animate 3D content.

problem: Skeleton-based temporal action segmentation faces conflicting feature requirements: classification needs temporal invariance while boundary localization requires temporal sensitivity.
approach: Proposes CurvSeg using curvature guidance from classification representations to localize boundaries, with dual-expert weighting mechanism for task-adaptive feature extraction.
contribution: Significantly improves temporal action segmentation by synergizing classification and localization through geometric curvature properties of skeleton sequences.

problem: Molecular docking via deep learning produces chemically implausible outputs and poor generalization due to complexity of modeling ligand-protein interactions.
approach: Proposes SigmaDock, an SE(3) Riemannian diffusion model that decomposes ligands into rigid-body fragments and learns to reassemble them within protein binding pockets.
contribution: Achieves 79.9% Top-1 success rates (RMSD <2 & PB-valid) on PoseBusters, first deep learning approach surpassing classical physics-based docking, with consistent generalization to unseen proteins.

problem: Test-time prompt tuning for vision-language models may lack sufficient angular diversity in textual feature distributions, hurting calibration performance.
approach: Proposes A-TPT, introducing angular diversity to encourage uniform distribution of normalized textual features on the unit hypersphere by maximizing minimum pairwise angular distances.
contribution: Consistently surpasses state-of-the-art TPT methods in reducing calibration error while maintaining comparable accuracy across various backbones and datasets.

problem: Average sensitivity as a simplicity metric lacks natural generalization to real-valued domains and fails to explain empirically observed junta-like input dependence in LLMs.
approach: Proposes noise stability as a comprehensive simplicity metric expressing model robustness to correlated noise across all input coordinates, with theoretical analysis for single-layer components.
contribution: Develops noise stability regularization that consistently accelerates training by 75% and catalyzes grokking, establishing noise stability as a powerful tool for understanding transformers.

problem: Simplicity bias in neural networks is widely observed but lacks a unifying theoretical framework across different architectures.
approach: Presents theoretical framework explaining simplicity bias through saddle-to-saddle learning dynamics, analyzing fixed points and invariant manifolds across fully-connected, convolutional, and attention architectures.
contribution: Shows neural networks learn increasingly complex solutions via iterative evolution near invariant manifolds and saddle-to-saddle transitions, unifying simplicity bias explanation.

problem: Existing vision-centric agent benchmarks use fully synthetic single-turn queries with limited visual modalities, lacking evaluation of multi-step reasoning in real-world settings.
approach: Introduces Agent-X, a benchmark with 828 authentic agentic tasks across six environments (visual reasoning, web browsing, security, autonomous driving, sports, math), with step-level evaluation framework.
contribution: Reveals even best-performing models (GPT, Gemini, Qwen families) achieve less than 50% full-chain success on multi-step vision tasks, identifying key reasoning and tool-use bottlenecks.

problem: Solving PDEs with operator learning overlooks spatially local information inherent in data, preventing full exploitation of local dynamics in physical phenomena.
approach: Proposes Riesz Neural Operator (RNO) based on spectral derivative representation using the Riesz transform to mix global spectral information with local directional variations.
contribution: RNO consistently achieves superior prediction accuracy and generalization compared to existing approaches across benchmark PDE problems and complex real-world datasets.

problem: Portfolio allocation in dynamic financial markets with shifting regimes requires balancing robust performance against changing market conditions and asset dynamics.
approach: Proposes STABLE, combining diffusion-based generative model for regime shifts with Black-Litterman estimation for portfolio allocation, using macroeconomic context and asset signals.
contribution: Generates regime-aware predictive return distributions reflecting macro regime while preserving firm-specific dynamics for improved risk-adjusted portfolio performance.

problem: Reasoning capabilities in LLMs depend on whether reasoning data is introduced during pretraining or post-training, with unclear effects of timing on performance and generalization.
approach: Conducts systematic study varying reasoning data scale, diversity, and quality across pretraining and post-training stages to measure performance impact.
contribution: Shows front-loading reasoning into pretraining is critical (19% average gain), establishing foundations that SFT cannot fully replicate; pretraining benefits from diversity while SFT prioritizes quality.

problem: Designing robust federated learning systems requires selecting, tuning, and combining complex strategies, resulting in brittle bespoke solutions.
approach: Introduces Helmsman, an LLM-based multi-agent framework automating end-to-end FL system synthesis through interactive planning, modular code generation, and closed-loop evaluation.
contribution: Generates FL solutions competitive with and often superior to established baselines on AgentFL-Bench (16 diverse tasks), advancing automated engineering of decentralized AI systems.

problem: Multimodal spatiotemporal learning on experimental data is constrained by sparse irregular noisy measurements with varying available modalities across space and time.
approach: Proposes OmniField, a continuity-aware framework learning continuous neural fields conditioned on available modalities with multimodal crosstalk architecture for iterative cross-modal refinement.
contribution: Consistently outperforms eight multimodal spatiotemporal baselines in reconstruction, interpolation, forecasting, and cross-modal prediction with robustness to sensor noise.

problem: Existing block-wise LLM quantization techniques incur suboptimal quantization errors and struggle with weight distribution mismatches.
approach: Proposes 4-bit Block-wise Optimal Float (BOF4) family of quantizers with optimization approach for block-wise quantization, signed absolute block maximum normalization (BOF4-S), and outlier-preserving quantization (OPQ).
contribution: BOF4-S consistently reduces quantization error compared to NF4 and AF4 with mixed-precision strategy (OPQ) achieving top performance in 4-bit block-wise quantization.

problem: Reliably evaluating LLM intelligence is challenging due to potential data contamination and benchmark overfitting in existing evaluation paradigms.
approach: Introduces LLM-as-a-Prophet paradigm and Prophet Arena benchmark that continuously collects live forecasting tasks decomposed into distinct pipeline stages for controlled evaluation.
contribution: Reveals frontier LLMs exhibit impressive forecasting capabilities but face bottlenecks including inaccurate event recalls, data source misunderstanding, and slower information aggregation than markets.
